newsitem.title: USA: Freightliner to build trucks in China.
newsitem.headline: Freightliner to build trucks in China.

text.p: Freightliner Corp Tuesday said it will become the first U.S. truck manufacturer to build heavy-duty trucks in China under a joint venture agreement.

Freightliner President and Chief Executive Officer James Hebe said the Freightliner heavy-duty truck joint venture will be located in Shanghai. The Shanghai partners are: Shanghai Zehai, an investment company representing five western provinces, and Shanghai Xijie, a local village development corporation.

Freightliner said it intends to market its FLD 112SD severe-duty aluminum conventional model to China -- first with completely built-up trucks or with local assembly of kits using a mix of U.S. and Chinese components, and later, with trucks built at its new Shanghai plant. The first phase is scheduled for completion in the fourth quarter of 1997.

Freightliner will target the "specialty" truck markets, which in China consists of tractors and trucks with bodies -- including dumps, tanks, mixers, refuse, fire and emergency vehicles, among others.
